- **Streams (static, ~22):** business, business_balance, entities, bills, bill_drafts, cards, departments, limits, locations, merchants, purchase_orders, receipts, reimbursements, spend_programs, transactions, users, vendors, statements, transfers, repayments, cashbacks, accounts, balance_history. `business`/`business_balance` are single-object. (`streams.py`)
- **Incremental:** none (no `replication_key`); server-side date filters only on first-page params: transactions/reimbursements `from_date`, bills `from_created_at` (from config `start_date`). BQ loader `overwrite: true`. (`streams.py:91-95,200-204,236-240`)
- **Record shaping:** per-stream `convert_to_string` JSON-stringifies nested fields (`stringify_complex_fields`) for flat BQ columns. (`base.py:56-57`)
- **Parity risk: LOW.** Straightforward paginated REST + OAuth2 client-credentials + per-stream date filter; maps cleanly to a generic REST source.

---

### BREX (corporate cards / spend)
- **Mechanism:** REST-JSON to `https://platform.brexapis.com`, Singer SDK `RESTStream` (`DriveRestStream`). (`base.py`)
- **Auth:** **static API key** as Bearer header (`APIKeyAuthenticator`, `Authorization: Bearer {api_key}`). No token exchange. (`base.py:38-46`)
- **Pagination:** cursor-in-body — `next_cursor` in response → `cursor` query param, `limit` up to 1000, records at `$.items[*]`. (`base.py:8-20,49-70`)
- **Streams (static, 6):** users (`/v2/users`), cards (`/v2/cards`), departments (`/v2/departments`), expenses (`/v1/expenses`), primary_card_account_transaction (`/v2/transactions/card/primary`), vendors (`/v1/vendors`). (`streams.py`)
- **Incremental:** none (no `replication_key`); full pull, BQ `overwrite: true`.
- **Record shaping:** `expand[]` query params to hydrate related objects (e.g. expenses expand location/department/merchant/user/budget/payment), `flatten_keys` (dict→`key_subkey`), `convert_to_string` (JSON-stringify). (`base.py:71-90`, `streams.py`)
- **Parity risk: LOW.** Clean cursor-paged REST with Bearer key; the only nuance is `expand[]` array query params.

---

### PLAID (bank-account aggregation)
- **Mechanism:** REST-JSON, **POST-only** to `https://{sandbox|production}.plaid.com` (env-dependent host). Uses raw `requests` via `DriveRestStream` — **NOT** the Plaid vendor SDK, despite the "Plaid" keyword in pyproject. `Plaid-Version` header pinned (default `2020-09-14`). (`base.py:118-165`)

- **Pagination:** cursor. transactions use `/transactions/sync`'s `has_more`+`next_cursor` (`PlaidSyncPaginator`); accounts are single-shot. (`streams.py:64-92`)
- **Streams (static, 2):** accounts (`POST /accounts/get`), transactions (`POST /transactions/sync`).
- **Plaid Item / access-token model:** one **partition per linked bank (Item)**. Config carries a single scalar `access_token`+`item_id` (a connection instance = one Item), wrapped into a one-element internal list; a deprecated `access_tokens` JSON-array fallback still supports multi-Item. STATE is partitioned by `item_id` (`state_partitioning_keys=["item_id"]`). (`base.py:60-165`, `streams.py`)
- **Incremental:** transactions use Plaid's **cursor sync** (not a timestamp key) — first run per Item = no cursor → full history; cursor saved to STATE **per page** (resumable mid-run); later runs send saved cursor for deltas. Emits `added`+`modified`; `removed` is logged but **not propagated** (upsert loader doesn't hard-delete — an explicit soft-delete gap). accounts are full-refresh (balances snapshot). `start_date` filter applied only on the first full run. (`streams.py:94-260`)

Fatal-vs-retriable Plaid error-code classification. (`base.py:8-20,254-296`, `streams.py`)

**Cross-cutting notes:** every tap does record shaping to flatten nested JSON into BQ-friendly flat string columns (either the tap's own `flatten_dict`/`convert_to_string`/`flatten_keys` or Singer post_process). **tap-intacct (Sage Intacct) — mechanism**

- **Source/category:** Sage Intacct — cloud ERP / accounting (GL, AP/AR, projects, contracts). Meltano Singer tap.
- **Mechanism (EXACT):** Sage Intacct XML Gateway / Web Services API. HTTP POST of XML bodies (built with `xmltodict.unparse`) to `https://api.intacct.com/ia/xml/xmlgw.phtml` (`const.py:196` `DEFAULT_API_URL`; login re-points to the per-tenant `endpoint` returned by getAPISession, `client.py:332`). Core data fetch uses the **modern `query` function** (`<query>` with `object`/`select`/`filter`/`pagesize`/`offset`/`orderby`) — see `client.py:635,733-743,937-948,1060-1073`. `readByQuery` is used ONLY in `get_sample` (`client.py:872-879`). **There is NO `readMore`/`resultId` flow** — a comment at `client.py:908-910,760-767` states the legacy `readByQuery`+`readMore(resultId)` chain was deliberately replaced by parallel offset pagination.
- **Auth:** Session-token, NOT HMAC. `control` block carries web-services partner `senderid`/`password` (`sender_id`/`sender_password`), and `operation.authentication.login` sends `userid`/`companyid`/`password`; `getAPISession` returns a `sessionid` used in subsequent calls' `authentication.sessionid` (`client.py:244-337,574`). A **session pool** (one sessionid per worker thread, `SESSION_POOL_SIZE=6`) is opened to defeat Intacct's per-session serialization (`client.py:222-322`).
- **Pagination:** Offset-based on `pagesize=2000`, ordered by `RECORDNO` (or `id` for `ORDER_BY_ID_STREAMS`) for stable order across concurrent pages. GLENTRY/GLBATCH use **bounded RECORDNO windows** (`WINDOW_SIZE=100000`, `RECORDNO > cursor AND <= cursor+WINDOW`) to avoid slow high offsets (`client.py:652-819`). Total count comes from `@totalcount` (`client.py:648`). Pages fetched concurrently via `_concurrent_fetch` (`client.py:122-151`).
- **Streams:** Dynamically discovered — schemas fetched per-object via the `lookup` function (`get_fields_data_using_schema_name`, `client.py:883-896`; `_load_schema_from_api`, `__init__.py:171-270`). Object set is static map `INTACCT_OBJECTS` (`const.py:100-164`); `streams_to_discover` config selects which (default `["class","department"]`, `const.py:198`). `audit_history` is fanned out into one `audit_history_<table>` stream per object (`__init__.py:744-755`). `gl_entry`/`gl_batch` get special two-phase handling; `additional_batches_to_sync` triggers `get_by_batch_numbers` for extra GL batches (`client.py:1016`, `__init__.py:483-571`).
- **Incremental/replication:** Bookmark = `WHENMODIFIED` (`GET_BY_DATE_FIELD="whenmodified"`, `const.py:194`) via a `greaterthanorequalto` filter (`client.py:627-632`); overrides in `REP_KEYS` (audit_history uses `accesstime`; several objects set `None` = full-table). GL windows filter on RECORDNO but still bookmark on the rep key. State written every 25k records (`__init__.py:680-685`).
- **Record shaping:** XML→dict via `xmltodict.parse`; keys normalized by `convert_record_keys` (`.`→`_`, lowercased, `utils.py:4-7`). `exclude_fields` (JSON map, per-stream) drops selected columns in `Context.get_selected_fields` (`__init__.py:73-84`); `ADDITIONAL_COLUMNS`/`STREAM_FIELD_WHITELIST` add/restrict. A synthetic `is_deleted` boolean is injected into every record/schema (`__init__.py:308-335`). No SQL-style joins in glentry.py/glbatch.py (service_type/service_status are separate lookup streams, not joined in-tap).
- **CRITICAL — correction to premise:** The tap does **NOT delete from (or write to) BigQuery.** `bigquery.py` issues only read-only `SELECT` queries. `gl_entry_deletion_lookback_days` / `gl_batch_deletion_lookback_days` drive `get_comparison_date` (`bigquery.py:40-50`, default 730 days) → `get_bq_recordnos` reads the rolling window of RECORDNOs currently in the BQ `gl_entry`/`gl_batch` table (`bigquery.py:53-93`). No `DELETE`/DML statement exists anywhere in bigquery.py. So it is a BQ-read-back soft-delete-detection mechanism, not a DELETE against BQ.
- **Parity risk (HIGH):** (1) Proprietary Intacct XML-gateway `query` syntax + windowed/offset pagination and `@totalcount` sizing — hard to reproduce faithfully. (2) Session-token auth with a multi-session pool and Intacct per-company concurrency caps (throttling/429/503/524 backoff, `client.py:339-355`). (3) The tap **reads back its own prior output from BigQuery** to compute soft-deletes — this couples the tap to the destination warehouse (requires `bigquery_project`/`dataset`/`credentials`; silently skips deletion detection if absent, `glentry.py:39-46`) and to the exact `gl_entry`/`gl_batch` table shape (`recordno`, `whenmodified`, `is_deleted` columns). (4) `is_deleted` synthetic column and audit-history-based deletion for non-GL streams add non-standard semantics.</result>

GET streams put `limit`/`offset` in query params (base.py:51-55); POST-query streams put `limit`/`offset` in the JSON body via `prepare_request_payload` (base.py:78-82). `AttioOffsetPaginator` advances by `page_size`, stops when a page returns `< page_size` rows (base.py:12-23); `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE=500`, notes capped at 50 (constants.py:2, streams.py:65).

Incremental/replication: `CreatedAtIncrementalMixin` sets `replication_key="created_at"`; adds POST body `filter: {created_at: {$gte: <bookmark>}}` + `sorts: created_at asc`, first run falls back to `start_date` (base.py:85-104). ## Summary of all six taps

Analysis complete for all 6. Key cross-cutting finding: **4 of 6 taps read/write BigQuery directly** (netsuite, quickbooks, xero DELETE from BQ; sage/intacct only READS BQ for soft-delete detection — the meltano config's "deletion" settings do **not** mean the tap deletes from BQ). netsuite_pro and salesforce are pure Singer stdout taps. Two "premise corrections" surfaced: netsuite_pro is OData v4 (not report-portal scraping), and tap-intacct does no DML against BQ.

### NetSuite (branch `feature-tap`) — ERP
- **Mechanism:** SuiteQL over SuiteTalk REST — POST `{"q":<SQL>}` to `/query/v1/suiteql` on `{account}.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/rest`; schema via metadata-catalog `/record/v1/metadata-catalog/`. No SOAP/RESTlet (zeep is a dead dep). (`objects/transaction.py:8`, `rest.py:98-101,485-582`)
- **Auth:** OAuth1 TBA, HMAC-SHA256 (consumer+token key/secret). (`rest.py:785-796`)
- **Pagination:** offset `limit=1000` to `hasMore=false`; adaptive ID-batch/date-window halving to dodge 99k offset ceiling. (`rest.py:896-938`, `switchrest.py:225`)
- **Streams:** static `ALL_STREAMS` + dynamic CustomTable; `streams_to_discover` selects. Parent→child: transaction-line streams enumerate changed+deleted txn IDs, refetch lines in 1000-ID `IN()` chunks. (`transaction_line.py:112-206`)
- **Incremental:** "switch" bookmark — ID-window sweep then flips to `lastmodifieddate`/`linelastmodifieddate`. (`switchrest.py:87-107`)
- **Shaping:** mostly pass-through; `MergedTransactionData` is a server-side SuiteQL JOIN+SUM+GROUP BY (computed grain). (`merged_transaction_data.py:36-101`)
- **Tap→BQ: YES.** `utils.cleanup_transactions_in_bq` `DELETE ... WHERE transaction IN UNNEST(@ids)` + reads BQ for deleted-ID resolution, before re-emit; 20k ID chunks, non-atomic. (`utils.py:84-224`, `transaction_line.py:72-77`)
- **Parity risk (HIGH):** stateful destination mutator; SuiteQL dialect + offset ceiling; non-idempotent fan-out; JOIN/SUM grain.

### NetSuite Pro — SuiteProjects Pro published reports
- **Mechanism:** OData v4 JSON REST — `GET /reports/{report_id}` on `{subdomain}.app.netsuitesuiteprojectspro.com/odata/v4`, records at `$.value[*]`. (README's OAuth2 claim is stale.) (`streams.py:24-64`)
- **Auth:** HTTP Basic, `base64(company_name\user:password)`. (`auth.py:15-18`)
- **Pagination:** OData `@odata.nextLink` → `$skiptoken` + `$top=1000`. (`streams.py:107-123`)
- **Streams:** dynamic — one stream per `reports` CSV entry (`report_id:report_name`). (`tap.py:51-66`)
- **Incremental:** NONE — full snapshot each run.
- **Shaping:** keys snake_cased; schema inferred from `$top=1`, all columns nullable string.
- **Tap→BQ: NO.** Standard stdout tap.
- **Parity risk:** low; all-string schema, no incremental, `split(":")` fragility.

### Salesforce — CRM (Stitch fork v1.9.0)
- **Mechanism:** `api_type: BULK` → Bulk API v1 (async job/batch, SOQL) — `POST /services/async/60.0/job` (queryAll, CSV), batch with SOQL, 20s poll, stream CSV. SOQL: `SELECT … WHERE <replkey> >= <start> ORDER BY <replkey> ASC`. Bulk2/REST present but inactive. 12-worker concurrency. (`salesforce/bulk.py:44,163-312`, `__init__.py:591-622`)

- **Tap→BQ: NO.**
- **Parity risk (HIGH):** Bulk-v1 async lifecycle + XML parse, PK-chunking + resumable state, SOQL generation, queryAll-includes-deleted, 12-way concurrency, pinned v60.0.

### QuickBooks (branch `feature-tap`) — QBO accounting (hotglue fork v1.4.54)
- **Mechanism:** QBO REST v3 — entities `GET /query?query=SELECT * FROM <E> STARTPOSITION n MAXRESULTS m` (minorversion 45); reports `GET /reports/<Name>` (minorversion 75). Host `/v3/company/<realmId>`. (`rest.py:34-168`, `rest_reports.py:97-103`)
- **Auth:** OAuth2 refresh_token (Intuit bearer, refresh 3300s, token rotated); `realmId` in path.
- **Pagination:** entities offset `STARTPOSITION`/`MAXRESULTS` (ladder 1000→50, `ORDERBY Id ASC`), separate deleted pass; reports date-windowed.
- **Streams:** entities from `QB_OBJECTS` filtered by `streams_to_discover`; 8 static report classes.

- **Parity risk (HIGH):** heuristic matrix flattening (minorversion-fragile); tap mutating BQ (wrong date_column dups/over-deletes; non-BQ targets uncleaned); offset dup/skip; date-window sizing changes emitted rows.

### Xero (branch `feature-tap`) — accounting (v2.3.2)

No DELETE/DML anywhere. (`bigquery.py:40-127`, `glentry.py:60`, `__init__.py:598-643`)
- **Parity risk (HIGH):** proprietary XML-gateway query + windowed/offset pagination + `@totalcount` sizing; multi-session-pool auth + Intacct concurrency caps; tap **reads back its own prior BQ output** to compute soft-deletes (couples tap to destination table shape; skips detection if BQ config absent); synthetic `is_deleted` semantics.</result>

- **Source/category:** Paylocity — payroll/HRIS.
- **Mechanism:** REST-JSON on Meltano SDK (`RESTStream`). Base `https://api.paylocity.com/api`. List `GET /v2/companies/{company_id}/employees`, detail `GET /v2/companies/{company_id}/employees/{employeeId}`; `parse_response` handles bare arrays and `{employees|data:[…]}` wrappers.

### Cross-cutting observations
- **All 7 are REST-JSON built on the Meltano/Singer SDK** (`RESTStream`). None use GraphQL, SOAP, or file/report-download transport (UKG explicitly *avoids* its SOAP `BIDataService` surface; BambooHR custom reports are JSON over REST, not file downloads).

- **Replication is overwhelmingly full-table** (BambooHR, ADP, iSolved, HiBob, Paylocity, Personio all full-refresh); **only UKG Pro** has genuine incremental streams (employee/payrollrun/employeepayrollrun). A generic OAuth2/Basic provider will not cover them without per-source customization.

# PART B — Sink: DrivetrainAi/target-bigquery (z3z1ma fork)

Effective config: `denormalized: true`, `method: batch_job`, `schema_resolver_version: "2"`, `column_name_transforms.add_underscore_when_invalid: true`, `cluster_on_key_properties: true`. Anthropic: `batch_size: 10000`, `upsert:[messages_usage,cost_report,api_key_costs,claude_code_usage]` + `overwrite:[api_keys,users,workspaces]` (disjoint). OpenAI: `batch_size: 10000`, `overwrite: true` (all streams). (The `batch_size: 5000` in the task prompt is not what the committed configs use.) Sink class resolved by `target.py:get_sink_class` → **`BigQueryBatchJobDenormalizedSink`** (`batch_job.py:137`).

## Table naming — `core.py:table_name` (lines 634–647)
From the **stream name**, unless `use_stream_name_as_table_name` is set (it is not here). Transform chain:
1. `stream.replace("-", "_").replace(".", "_")`
2. `camel_to_snake(name, seperate_letter_and_number_in_table_name=True)` (`core.py:1567`) — inserts `_` between camelCase boundaries **and between letters↔digits** (e.g. `foo2` → `foo_2`).
3. collapse repeated `_` → single, strip leading/trailing `_`, `.lower()`.

These stream names are already snake_case, so tables are essentially identical to the stream name: `api_keys`, `messages_usage`, `cost_report`, `claude_code_usage`, `completions_usage`, `costs`, `project_api_keys`, etc. **No dataset prefix/suffix** — dataset comes from the `dataset` config; table = derived name. **Parity gotcha**: the letter↔digit split (`separate_letter_and_number=True` default) — any stream name with an adjacent letter/digit would get an underscore inserted.

## Column mapping — `SchemaTranslator` (`core.py:1129`), `denormalized: true`
Denormalized = **one flat top-level BQ column per top-level JSON-schema property** (`Denormalized.preprocess_record` → `translate_record`, `core.py:960`; contrast fixed-schema mode which wraps everything in one `data` JSON column). Column names run through `transform_column_name`.

**`schema_resolver_version: "2"`** (`_jsonschema_property_to_bigquery_column`, V2 branch lines 1244–1294): far more lenient than V1 — **falls back to `JSON` for anything unresolvable** instead of erroring. Behavior:
- `anyOf` → uses index [0]’s type/format.
- **array**: no `items`/no item `type`/`patternProperties` → `JSON REPEATED`; item type record → `RECORD REPEATED`; else scalar `<type> REPEATED`.
- **object**: no `properties`, empty `properties`, or `patternProperties` present → **`JSON NULLABLE`** (whole object stored as a JSON value); otherwise recurse into a `RECORD` with nested fields (`_translate_record_to_bigquery_schema`, line 1298 — empty props → `JSON`).
- **scalar**: `patternProperties` → `JSON`; else `bigquery_type()`.
- On **any exception** → `JSON NULLABLE` (with a table/field-name special-case in `IGNORE_JSON_FIELDS_FOR_TABLES` → `STRING`).

So nested objects **with a declared schema** become native BQ `RECORD` (STRUCT); schemaless/dynamic objects and arrays-of-unknown become `JSON`; arrays of scalars/records become `REPEATED`. (For these taps most objects are pre-flattened/typed, so expect mostly scalar columns + a few RECORD/JSON.)

**Type map — `bigquery_type` (`core.py:1498`)**: `format:date-time`→`TIMESTAMP`; `date`→`DATE`; `time`→`TIME`; `number`→`FLOAT`; `integer`+`string`→`STRING`; `integer`→`INTEGER`; `boolean`→`BOOLEAN`; `object`→`RECORD`; **else `STRING`** (default/unknown). All scalar fields land `NULLABLE`.

**`column_name_transforms.add_underscore_when_invalid: true`** — `transform_column_name` (`core.py:1524`): strips backticks; removes Unicode whitespace/control/zero-width chars; **if first char is a digit, prepends `_`** (the "add_underscore_when_invalid" behavior); replaces `.`→`_` (`replace_period_with_underscore` is force-set True in translation, lines 1156/1167); and **always** replaces special chars `[!@#$%^&*()/,]`→`_`. Note: `lower`/`snake_case` are **not** enabled by this config, so column casing is preserved as-is from the tap (only the invalid-char/leading-digit fixes apply). The function is `@cache`d.

## `_sdc_` metadata columns — `constants.py:DEFAULT_SCHEMA` / `SDC_FIELDS`; added by `preprocess_record` (`core.py:669`)
Every record gets exactly these 6 system columns popped out and attached (order as emitted). In denormalized mode they sit **alongside** the flat data columns (in fixed mode they accompany the single `data` JSON column):

| Column | BQ type |
|---|---|
| `_sdc_extracted_at` | TIMESTAMP |
| `_sdc_received_at` | TIMESTAMP |
| `_sdc_batched_at` | TIMESTAMP |
| `_sdc_deleted_at` | TIMESTAMP |
| `_sdc_sequence` | INT64 |
| `_sdc_table_version` | INTEGER |

No other system columns (no `_sdc_primary_key`, no `_sdc_received_at`-style extras beyond the above). **For byte-identical tables faucet-sink-bigquery must add these six columns, with these exact names/types, populated with the same semantics** (extracted_at from the tap's record `time_extracted`; received_at/batched_at = target-side timestamps; sequence = ms epoch ordering; deleted_at usually null; table_version usually null for these taps).

## Load method — `batch_job` (`batch_job.py`) + `load_with_retry` (`core.py:1051`)
- **Direct BigQuery load job, no GCS staging** (GCS is a separate `gcs_stage` method). Records are serialized to **newline-delimited JSON** (`orjson.dumps`, `process_record`), buffered and **gzip-compressed in memory** (`Compressor`), then loaded via `client.load_table_from_file(BytesIO(data), …)`.
- `LoadJobConfig` (denormalized, `batch_job.py:139`): `source_format = NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON`, `write_disposition = WRITE_APPEND`, `schema_update_options = [ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION]`, `ignore_unknown_values = True`, explicit `schema = table.get_resolved_schema()`. One load job per batch (`batch_size`); parallelism via worker pool (`options.max_workers: 1` here → single worker).
- Retries transient job errors up to 3×.

**`overwrite` (WRITE_TRUNCATE full replace) — staging + swap:**
1. On init (`core.py:414`, `_is_overwrite_candidate` supports bool `true` OR fnmatch list), the real table is created (`create_target`), then `self.table` is repointed to a **staging table** `{name}__{YYYYMMDDHHMMSS}__{uuid}` (`_create_overwrite_table`, line 424; expires in `staging_table_expiration_days`, default 3).
2. All batches WRITE_APPEND into staging.
3. `clean_up` (`core.py:872`): a **`WRITE_TRUNCATE` query job** `SELECT * FROM staging` → destination = the real `overwrite_target` (atomic full replace; kept as a query job, not DDL, so it works on partitioned tables). If `key_properties` exist it **dedups**: `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY <keys> ORDER BY _sdc_extracted_at DESC, _sdc_received_at DESC)=1`. Then drops staging. Optional `overwrite_min_row_ratio` shrink guard can refuse a suspiciously small snapshot.
4. State is **withheld** until the swap completes (`defers_state`, `core.py:742`) so an interrupted run never advances the bookmark past unwritten rows.

**`upsert` (MERGE on key_properties) — staging + MERGE** (`_is_upsert_candidate`, line 448; only when `key_properties` present AND denormalized):
- Staging table receives batches; `merge_table` (`core.py:765`) runs `MERGE target USING staging ON target.<k>=source.<k> (AND … per key) WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET <all matching cols> WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (…)`, then drops staging. Runs in `pre_state_hook` (before each state msg) and `clean_up`. Optional `dedupe_before_upsert` wraps the source in the same QUALIFY dedup.
- **`upsert` wins over `overwrite`** if a stream matches both (`__init__` checks upsert first); a stream with no `key_properties` falls through (upsert ignored).

## Clustering / partitioning — `create_target` (`core.py:690`) + `default_table_options` (`core.py:264`)
- **`cluster_on_key_properties: true`** → `clustering_fields = tuple(key_properties[:4])` (first 4 PKs; BQ's max). Falls back to default `["_sdc_batched_at"]` when a stream has no key_properties.
- **Partitioning**: no `partition_granularity` is configured, so the **default applies: `TimePartitioning(type=MONTH, field="_sdc_batched_at")`** (from `default_table_options`, merged in `as_table`). So every table is **month-partitioned on `_sdc_batched_at`** and clustered on the first ≤4 key columns. (If `partition_granularity` were set it would still partition on `_sdc_batched_at`, only changing the grain.)
- Staging tables inherit the same defaults; the final overwrite/merge writes into the pre-created real table which already carries the intended partition/cluster spec.

**Parity checklist for faucet-sink-bigquery to produce identical tables:**
1. Table name = snake_cased/letter-digit-split stream name (see naming rules), in the configured dataset, no prefix.
2. Denormalized flat columns from top-level JSON-schema props, typed via the V2 resolver rules (JSON fallback for unresolvable; RECORD for typed nested objects; REPEATED for arrays; TIMESTAMP/DATE/TIME/FLOAT/INTEGER/BOOLEAN/STRING per `bigquery_type`), names transformed with leading-digit `_` prefix + special-char→`_` + `.`→`_` (no lowercasing).
3. Append the **six `_sdc_*` columns** with exact names/types/semantics above.
4. Month-partition on `_sdc_batched_at`; cluster on `key_properties[:4]` (or `_sdc_batched_at` if none).
5. Load as gzipped NDJSON via a load job (WRITE_APPEND), with `ignore_unknown_values` + `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION`.
6. For overwrite: stage → dedup-by-key (`_sdc_extracted_at`/`_sdc_received_at` DESC) → `WRITE_TRUNCATE` swap; for upsert: stage → `MERGE` on keys. Note upsert-wins-over-overwrite tie-break.

Files cited: `target_bigquery/constants.py` (`DEFAULT_SCHEMA`, `SDC_FIELDS`), `target_bigquery/core.py` (`BigQueryTable`, `BaseBigQuerySink.__init__/_create_overwrite_table/_is_upsert_candidate/_is_overwrite_candidate/table_name/preprocess_record/create_target/merge_table/clean_up`, `Denormalized`, `SchemaTranslator`, `bigquery_type`, `transform_column_name`, `camel_to_snake`), `target_bigquery/batch_job.py` (`BigQueryBatchJobDenormalizedSink.job_config/process_record/process_batch`, `load_with_retry`), `target_bigquery/target.py` (`get_sink_class`, upsert/overwrite config docs).

## tap-shopify
Files: `tap_shopify/base.py`, `streams.py`, `tap.py`, `queries.py`, `constants.py`
- **Source/category:** Shopify — e-commerce platform (orders/customers/products/analytics).

All streams subclass `singer_sdk.GraphQLStream`; POST `{query, variables}`. Two flavors: Admin GraphQL connections + **ShopifyQL** analytics via the `shopifyqlQuery` field (a proprietary SQL-like DSL).

1. `stream.replace("-", "_").replace(".", "_")`

These stream names are already snake_case, so tables are essentially identical to the stream name: `api_keys`, `messages_usage`, `cost_report`, `claude_code_usage`, `completions_usage`, `costs`, `project_api_keys`, etc. **No dataset prefix/suffix** — dataset comes from the `dataset` config; table = derived name. **Parity gotcha**: the letter↔digit split (`separate_letter_and_number=True` default) — any stream name with an adjacent letter/digit would get an underscore inserted.

- **array**: no `items`/no item `type`/`patternProperties` → `JSON REPEATED`; item type record → `RECORD REPEATED`; else scalar `<type> REPEATED`.

| `_sdc_extracted_at` | TIMESTAMP |

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* — most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token — a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Before publishing, scan the stylesheet for any color declared only inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — that is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

Migration analysis · Drivetrain data platform

Replacing the Meltano taps with faucet-stream

Can faucet-stream drop into DrivetrainAi/meltano_taps — 46 sources, all landing in one BigQuery target — and produce the same raw tables? Here is the per-source verdict, and the one thing that gates every row.

Scope: 46 taps · sink: z3z1ma target-bigquery (denormalized, batch_job) · goal: in-place replace, byte-identical BigQuery tables · note: Singer is excluded by design — verdicts use each tap's actual transport (REST / OData / GraphQL / SQL / SOAP / file).

3
Clean source
Reproducible today with a stock connector.
18
With work
Config + faucet transforms / matrix fan-out.
20
Partial
Custom auth, dynamic schema, or some streams blocked.
5
Blocked
Bulk / SDK / SOAP-XLSX / tap↔BigQuery coupling.

⚠ The verdicts above are source-side. Byte-identical tables are gated by the sink — for every row.

The taps all load through one shared target, the z3z1ma target-bigquery fork, in denormalized + batch_job mode. That target does a lot to each table that faucet-sink-bigquery does not do today:

• Auto-creates a denormalized flat schema from the stream's JSON schema (V2 resolver: JSON fallback, RECORD for typed nested, REPEATED arrays). • Adds six _sdc_* system columns to every table — _sdc_extracted_at / received_at / batched_at / deleted_at (TIMESTAMP), _sdc_sequence (INT64), _sdc_table_version (INTEGER). • Applies column-name transforms (leading-digit → _, special chars → _, . → _; no lower-casing). • Month-partitions on _sdc_batched_at and clusters on key_properties[:4]. • Loads gzipped NDJSON load jobs; overwrite = stage → dedup-by-key → WRITE_TRUNCATE swap; upsert = stage → MERGE.

faucet-sink-bigquery today inserts typed columns into a pre-existing table (streaming / MERGE / overwrite-swap, all shipped) but emits no _sdc_ columns, no auto-denormalized schema, no column sanitization, and no month-on-_sdc_batched_at partition/cluster.

Bottom line: a "Singer-compatibility" mode on faucet-sink-bigquery is the single prerequisite for every table to match. Without it, no source is byte-identical; with it, the ~21 green/amber rows below become true drop-in replacements.

01Per-source parity matrix

All 46 taps. Verdict is source-side (transport, auth, fan-out, shaping) assuming the sink-compatibility work above is done. Filter by verdict; the left stripe encodes severity.

SourceMechanismAuthFan-out / streamsVerdictWhat decides it

Verdict key — Clean: stock faucet connector + light config. With work: reproducible via faucet transforms + matrix fan-out/discovery and/or a supported-but-fiddly auth. Partial: custom multi-step auth, per-tenant dynamic schema, or bespoke shaping — approximable with the SQL/WASM transforms but exact parity is hard, or a subset of streams (usually reports) is blocked. Blocked: async bulk, vendor SDK, SOAP-with-embedded-XLSX, or the tap reaches into BigQuery mid-sync — not reproducible by a declarative source→sink pipeline.

02What faucet-stream already covers

Most of the transport, auth and fan-out surface these taps use maps directly onto shipped faucet-stream capabilities — several of them landed in the recent PRs.

Transport

  • REST-JSON — the rest source most taps
  • OData v2/v4 — rest + NextLinkInBody pagination sap · d365 · r365
  • GraphQL — the graphql source shopify
  • SQL warehouse — redshift source redshift
  • Authed CSV / Excel files — rest response_format: csv|excel (#497) sharepoint · onedrive

Auth

  • Bearer / Basic / API-key / custom header ✓
  • OAuth2 client-credentials & refresh, with rotated-token persistence (#499) ✓
  • OAuth1 HMAC-SHA256 (#496) netsuite TBA
  • Mutual TLS client certs (#495) adp
  • Token-endpoint w/ JSONPath token personio envelope

Fan-out & scheduling

  • Static stream matrix + deep merge ✓
  • Parent→child N+1 fan-out pervasive
  • Discovery cross-product (#501) d365-bc · rillet · dualentry
  • Date/period windows — ${now.*} + backfill reports
  • SQL catalog discovery (#211) redshift

Shaping & write

  • flatten · keys_case · select/drop/set/cast · explode ✓
  • SQL / WASM transforms for unpivot, joins, computed cols approximate
  • write_mode: overwrite full-refresh swap (#492) most taps
  • write_mode: upsert + dedup (#224) incremental taps

03The blockers faucet can't reproduce declaratively

These patterns are architectural, not config gaps — they're why the 5 red rows are red and why several "partial" rows lose their report streams.

1Tap ↔ BigQuery coupling

  • netsuite, quickbooks, xero, zohobooks DELETE a rolling window from the destination before re-emitting; sage reads prior BQ output to compute soft-deletes.
  • The tap is a stateful destination mutator. A clean source→sink pipeline never reaches back into the warehouse mid-extract, so these report/incremental streams cannot match.

2Async / bulk / vendor SDK

  • salesforce — Bulk API v1 (create job → poll → download CSV, PK-chunk resume).
  • stripe — official Python SDK + Events-API-as-incremental + async report-run/CSV.
  • Not a paginated-GET pattern; faucet's REST source can't drive the job lifecycle.

3Runtime-synthesized schema

  • hubspot builds stream classes at runtime for custom objects/associations/history + a 10k-result id workaround.
  • Per-tenant dynamic columns: bamboohr custom reports, hibob metadata, personio, ukg UDFs, campfire custom fields.

4Bespoke report shaping

  • rillet hand-flattens a hierarchical report tree with reconciliation rules + elimination-entity unions.
  • quickbooks / xero flatten a Rows/Columns matrix; oracle_fusion parses a base64 XLSX out of a SOAP body.

5Multi-step / signed auth

  • bullhorn refresh→access→login→BhRestToken + dynamic base URL; sap, acumatica cookie-session login; sage session pool; skyslope HMAC + session.
  • faucet's auth providers are single-step; these need a session/pre-flight provider.

6Exact record-shape fidelity

  • Every tap flattens to parent_child columns and JSON-stringifies nested fields with a specific delimiter/rule set.
  • "Same table" means matching that column set and the six _sdc_ columns exactly — reproducible, but it's per-tap transform work, not free.

04What to build for full parity

In priority order. Item 1 unblocks every row; the rest expand how many taps reach true drop-in status.

  1. faucet-sink-bigquery "Singer-compat" mode — prerequisite for all 46

    Auto-denormalized schema from inferred JSON schema (V2 rules), the six _sdc_* columns with matching semantics, z3z1ma column-name transforms, month-partition on _sdc_batched_at + cluster on keys, and gzipped-NDJSON load jobs with staged overwrite-dedup / MERGE. Nothing is byte-identical without this.

  2. Session / pre-flight auth provider — unlocks bullhorn · sap · acumatica · sage · skyslope

    A shared provider that runs a login step, captures a token/cookie/dynamic base-URL, and re-authenticates on 401 — modelled like the existing oauth2_refresh provider.

  3. Bookmark → request-parameter injection — server-side incremental

    Let the stored bookmark flow into a query param / filter (Lucene range, gte|, OData $filter, If-Modified-Since). Today faucet filters incremental client-side.

  4. Report/matrix flattening recipes — rillet · qbo · xero reports

    Ship SQL/WASM transform templates for report-tree and Rows/Columns-matrix flattening. Still can't match streams that also delete-from-BigQuery.

  5. Async-job source pattern — salesforce bulk · stripe reports

    A source shape that submits a job, polls, and downloads the result (CSV). Larger effort; only two taps need it.

05Suggested rollout

Once the sink-compat mode exists, migrate in waves of decreasing determinism.

Wave 1 Clean & with-work

21 taps — stock connector + config/transforms, mostly full-refresh overwrite (easiest to prove identical).

  • ramp, brex, invoiced, redshift, netsuite_pro, ms365fno, ms365bc, afas, dualentry, deskera, restaurant365, campfire, adp, isolved, paylocity, rippling, greenhouse, lever, navan, anthropic, openai

Wave 2 Partial

20 taps — need a session-auth provider, dynamic-schema handling, or per-tap shaping recipes; validate table-by-table.

  • sap, syteline, acumatica, sharepointsites, onedrive, shopify, plaid, bamboohr, hibob, personio, ukg_pro, deel, bullhorn, skyslope, attio, quickbooks*, xero*, zohobooks*, sage*, rillet* (*entity streams only; report streams blocked)

Hold Blocked

5 taps — keep on Meltano until the async-job / session patterns land, or accept a non-identical rebuild.

  • salesforce (bulk API), stripe (SDK + events + reports), netsuite (SuiteQL + BQ mutation), hubspot (runtime streams + BQ side-channel), oracle_fusion (SOAP + XLSX)

Method — each of the 46 DrivetrainAi/tap-* repositories was read directly (transport, auth, pagination, stream/fan-out model, incremental strategy, in-tap record shaping), alongside the shared target-bigquery fork to pin the exact table contract. Verdicts assume the sink-compatibility work in §04 item 1; they describe reproducing each tap's output, not merely calling the same API. "Blocked" means not reproducible by a declarative source→sink pipeline without new faucet capabilities, not that the source is unreachable.

faucet-sink-bigquery today inserts typed columns into a pre-existing table (streaming / MERGE / overwrite-swap, all shipped) but emits no _sdc_ columns, no auto-denormalized schema, no column sanitization, and no month-on-_sdc_batched_at partition/cluster.

Bottom line: a "Singer-compatibility" mode on faucet-sink-bigquery is the single prerequisite for every table to match. Without it, no source is byte-identical; with it, the ~21 green/amber rows below become true drop-in replacements.

01Per-source parity matrix

All 46 taps. Verdict is source-side (transport, auth, fan-out, shaping) assuming the sink-compatibility work above is done. Filter by verdict; the left stripe encodes severity.

SourceMechanismAuthFan-out / streamsVerdictWhat decides it

Verdict key — Clean: stock faucet connector + light config. With work: reproducible via faucet transforms + matrix fan-out/discovery and/or a supported-but-fiddly auth. Partial: custom multi-step auth, per-tenant dynamic schema, or bespoke shaping — approximable with the SQL/WASM transforms but exact parity is hard, or a subset of streams (usually reports) is blocked. Blocked: async bulk, vendor SDK, SOAP-with-embedded-XLSX, or the tap reaches into BigQuery mid-sync — not reproducible by a declarative source→sink pipeline.

02What faucet-stream already covers

Most of the transport, auth and fan-out surface these taps use maps directly onto shipped faucet-stream capabilities — several of them landed in the recent PRs.

Transport

  • REST-JSON — the rest source most taps
  • OData v2/v4 — rest + NextLinkInBody pagination sap · d365 · r365
  • GraphQL — the graphql source shopify
  • SQL warehouse — redshift source redshift
  • Authed CSV / Excel files — rest response_format: csv|excel (#497) sharepoint · onedrive

Auth

  • Bearer / Basic / API-key / custom header ✓
  • OAuth2 client-credentials & refresh, with rotated-token persistence (#499) ✓
  • OAuth1 HMAC-SHA256 (#496) netsuite TBA
  • Mutual TLS client certs (#495) adp
  • Token-endpoint w/ JSONPath token personio envelope

Fan-out & scheduling

  • Static stream matrix + deep merge ✓
  • Parent→child N+1 fan-out pervasive
  • Discovery cross-product (#501) d365-bc · rillet · dualentry
  • Date/period windows — ${now.*} + backfill reports
  • SQL catalog discovery (#211) redshift

Shaping & write

  • flatten · keys_case · select/drop/set/cast · explode ✓
  • SQL / WASM transforms for unpivot, joins, computed cols approximate
  • write_mode: overwrite full-refresh swap (#492) most taps
  • write_mode: upsert + dedup (#224) incremental taps

03The blockers faucet can't reproduce declaratively

These patterns are architectural, not config gaps — they're why the 5 red rows are red and why several "partial" rows lose their report streams.

1Tap ↔ BigQuery coupling

  • netsuite, quickbooks, xero, zohobooks DELETE a rolling window from the destination before re-emitting; sage reads prior BQ output to compute soft-deletes.
  • The tap is a stateful destination mutator. A clean source→sink pipeline never reaches back into the warehouse mid-extract, so these report/incremental streams cannot match.

2Async / bulk / vendor SDK

  • salesforce — Bulk API v1 (create job → poll → download CSV, PK-chunk resume).
  • stripe — official Python SDK + Events-API-as-incremental + async report-run/CSV.
  • Not a paginated-GET pattern; faucet's REST source can't drive the job lifecycle.

3Runtime-synthesized schema

  • hubspot builds stream classes at runtime for custom objects/associations/history + a 10k-result id workaround.
  • Per-tenant dynamic columns: bamboohr custom reports, hibob metadata, personio, ukg UDFs, campfire custom fields.

4Bespoke report shaping

  • rillet hand-flattens a hierarchical report tree with reconciliation rules + elimination-entity unions.
  • quickbooks / xero flatten a Rows/Columns matrix; oracle_fusion parses a base64 XLSX out of a SOAP body.

5Multi-step / signed auth

  • bullhorn refresh→access→login→BhRestToken + dynamic base URL; sap, acumatica cookie-session login; sage session pool; skyslope HMAC + session.
  • faucet's auth providers are single-step; these need a session/pre-flight provider.

6Exact record-shape fidelity

  • Every tap flattens to parent_child columns and JSON-stringifies nested fields with a specific delimiter/rule set.
  • "Same table" means matching that column set and the six _sdc_ columns exactly — reproducible, but it's per-tap transform work, not free.

04What to build for full parity

In priority order. Item 1 unblocks every row; the rest expand how many taps reach true drop-in status.

  1. faucet-sink-bigquery "Singer-compat" mode — prerequisite for all 46

    Auto-denormalized schema from inferred JSON schema (V2 rules), the six _sdc_* columns with matching semantics, z3z1ma column-name transforms, month-partition on _sdc_batched_at + cluster on keys, and gzipped-NDJSON load jobs with staged overwrite-dedup / MERGE. Nothing is byte-identical without this.

  2. Session / pre-flight auth provider — unlocks bullhorn · sap · acumatica · sage · skyslope

    A shared provider that runs a login step, captures a token/cookie/dynamic base-URL, and re-authenticates on 401 — modelled like the existing oauth2_refresh provider.

  3. Bookmark → request-parameter injection — server-side incremental

    Let the stored bookmark flow into a query param / filter (Lucene range, gte|, OData $filter, If-Modified-Since). Today faucet filters incremental client-side.

  4. Report/matrix flattening recipes — rillet · qbo · xero reports

    Ship SQL/WASM transform templates for report-tree and Rows/Columns-matrix flattening. Still can't match streams that also delete-from-BigQuery.

  5. Async-job source pattern — salesforce bulk · stripe reports

    A source shape that submits a job, polls, and downloads the result (CSV). Larger effort; only two taps need it.

05Suggested rollout

Once the sink-compat mode exists, migrate in waves of decreasing determinism.

Wave 1 Clean & with-work

21 taps — stock connector + config/transforms, mostly full-refresh overwrite (easiest to prove identical).

  • ramp, brex, invoiced, redshift, netsuite_pro, ms365fno, ms365bc, afas, dualentry, deskera, restaurant365, campfire, adp, isolved, paylocity, rippling, greenhouse, lever, navan, anthropic, openai

Wave 2 Partial

20 taps — need a session-auth provider, dynamic-schema handling, or per-tap shaping recipes; validate table-by-table.

  • sap, syteline, acumatica, sharepointsites, onedrive, shopify, plaid, bamboohr, hibob, personio, ukg_pro, deel, bullhorn, skyslope, attio, quickbooks*, xero*, zohobooks*, sage*, rillet* (*entity streams only; report streams blocked)

Hold Blocked

5 taps — keep on Meltano until the async-job / session patterns land, or accept a non-identical rebuild.

  • salesforce (bulk API), stripe (SDK + events + reports), netsuite (SuiteQL + BQ mutation), hubspot (runtime streams + BQ side-channel), oracle_fusion (SOAP + XLSX)

Method — each of the 46 DrivetrainAi/tap-* repositories was read directly (transport, auth, pagination, stream/fan-out model, incremental strategy, in-tap record shaping), alongside the shared target-bigquery fork to pin the exact table contract. Verdicts assume the sink-compatibility work in §04 item 1; they describe reproducing each tap's output, not merely calling the same API. "Blocked" means not reproducible by a declarative source→sink pipeline without new faucet capabilities, not that the source is unreachable.

Analysis complete — artifact published: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/8af1e9fd-2eb6-497d-a7ad-5a3b16fa004d** (private; a filterable per-source matrix you can share with the team).

## What I found

I read all **46 `DrivetrainAi/tap-*` repos** directly (not the Singer wrapper — each tap's real transport, auth, pagination, fan-out, incremental strategy, and in-tap record shaping) plus the shared `target-bigquery` fork to pin the exact table contract.

**The headline: the sink gates everything.** Every tap loads through z3z1ma `target-bigquery` in `denormalized` + `batch_job` mode, which does a lot faucet-sink-bigquery doesn't do today: auto-builds a denormalized flat schema, adds **six `_sdc_*` columns**, applies specific column-name transforms, **month-partitions on `_sdc_batched_at` + clusters on keys**, and loads gzipped-NDJSON jobs with staged overwrite-dedup / MERGE. Until faucet-sink-bigquery gets a "Singer-compatibility" mode, **no** table is byte-identical — regardless of how well the source is reproduced.

**Source-side verdicts (46 taps):**
- **3 clean** (ramp, brex, invoiced) — stock `rest` source.
- **18 with work** — faucet transforms + matrix fan-out/discovery and a supported auth. Notably these lean on capabilities I just shipped: OData→`NextLinkInBody`, OAuth1 (#496), mTLS (#495), oauth2-refresh persist (#499), discovery cross-product (#501), CSV/Excel file source (#497), overwrite (#492).
- **20 partial** — custom session-auth (bullhorn/sap/acumatica/sage/skyslope), per-tenant dynamic schema (hubspot-lite cases), or report streams blocked.
- **5 blocked** — architectural: salesforce (bulk API), stripe (SDK + events + report CSV), netsuite (SuiteQL + mutates BigQuery mid-sync), hubspot (runtime-synthesized streams + direct-BQ side channel), oracle_fusion (SOAP → base64 XLSX).

**Biggest non-obvious blocker:** several taps (netsuite, quickbooks, xero, zohobooks, sage) **reach into BigQuery mid-extract** (rolling-window DELETE, or read-back for soft-deletes). A clean source→sink pipeline can't reproduce that coupling, so their report/incremental streams can't be made identical.

The artifact lays out the per-source matrix, faucet's coverage, the six blocker classes, a prioritized "what to build" list (sink-compat mode first), and a three-wave rollout.

One caveat worth stating plainly: these verdicts describe reproducing each tap's *output shape*, and the deeper record-shaping fidelity (exact flattened column names + the `_sdc_` set) is per-tap transform work even on the green rows — real, but not free.

Important correction from the sink code: faucet-sink-bigquery **already** loads via BigQuery load jobs with `create_disposition: CREATE_IF_NEEDED`, does overwrite-swap preserving partition/clustering, MERGE upsert, and schema-evolution (ALTER ADD COLUMN). Let me file the `_faucet` columns idea as an issue (per repo policy) and then revise the artifact.

input.command:
cd /Users/c-sikawats/Documents/GitHub/Personal/faucet-stream
gh auth switch --user PawanSikawat >/dev/null 2>&1
gh issue create --repo faucet-hq/faucet-stream \
  --title "feat(sink): optional \`_faucet_*\` run/lineage metadata columns" \
  --label feature --label tier-3 \
  --body "$(cat <<'MSG'
## Summary
Add an opt-in set of `_faucet_*` metadata columns that sinks stamp onto every row — the faucet-native analogue of Singer's `_sdc_*` columns, for lineage/debugging and Meltano-replacement parity.

## Motivation
Analysing the Drivetrain `meltano_taps` fleet (goal: replace Meltano taps with faucet-stream producing the same BigQuery tables), the z3z1ma `target-bigquery` adds six `_sdc_*` columns to every table (`_sdc_extracted_at/received_at/batched_at/deleted_at`, `_sdc_sequence`, `_sdc_table_version`). Drivetrain does **not** need those preserved, but a lightweight faucet-native equivalent is valuable for:
- **Freshness / lineage**: "when was this row extracted vs loaded, by which run".
- **Debugging + incident triage**: attributing rows to a run id / source.
- **Soft-delete & incremental audit** without coupling the connector to the destination.

Ties back to the Primary Goal (reliability/observability) and to being a credible drop-in for Singer/Meltano targets.

## Proposed design (sketch — needs design discussion)
A top-level opt-in block (pipeline-level, applied by the sink decorator so every sink benefits), e.g.:

```yaml
metadata_columns:
  enabled: true
  prefix: "_faucet"          # column name prefix
  columns: [extracted_at, loaded_at, run_id, source]   # subset selectable
```

Candidate columns:
- `_faucet_extracted_at` (TIMESTAMP) — when the source produced the record (page fetch time).
- `_faucet_loaded_at` (TIMESTAMP) — sink write time.
- `_faucet_run_id` (STRING) — the pipeline run id.
- `_faucet_source` (STRING) — connector kind / stream id.
- (optional) `_faucet_sequence` (INT64) — monotonic ordering within a run.

Likely implemented as a **core sink decorator** (like `CleanupTracker`) that injects the columns before `write_batch`, so it is connector-agnostic and works for bigquery/postgres/jsonl/etc. — not a per-connector feature. Column types must map cleanly per sink (TIMESTAMP/STRING/INT64).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/core` (a `metadata`/decorator module + `Pipeline::with_metadata_columns`), the CLI config block + expand wiring, docs. No connector changes if done as a decorator.

## Edge cases & failure modes
- Name collision with a real source field → error at config-load, or namespaced prefix avoids it.
- Determinism for exactly-once / overwrite dedup (should `_faucet_loaded_at` participate in dedup ordering? probably yes, like `_sdc` does).
- Redaction boundary (these are non-secret, safe to log).

- Opt-in; off by default (zero overhead when unset).

The rest of z3z1ma's "denormalized" shape is reproducible on the source side with inbuilt transforms: flatten → parent_child columns, keys_case → snake_case, rename_keys/rename_field for aliases, set for injected columns (company/env/parent-ids), cast for epoch↔timestamp. Two small sink follow-ups remain (not blockers): match z3z1ma's type-mapping rules (e.g. integer+string → STRING, JSON fallback for schemaless objects), and expose partition/cluster config (today it preserves a pre-created table's spec). And one ubiquitous shaping step — JSON-stringifying a nested field — has no inbuilt transform yet, so it currently falls to SQL; a one-line json_encode transform would keep those rows inbuilt-only (see §04).

01Per-source parity matrix

All 46 taps, re-scored. Supported = stock connector + inbuilt transforms. Needs SQL = the DuckDB transform is required (and is fine by your rules) — the exact reshape is named. Partial/Blocked are not shaping problems — they're auth, transport, dynamic-stream, or destination-coupling gaps that neither SQL nor WASM would fix.

SourceMechanismAuthFan-out / streamsVerdictWhat decides it

Every row also assumes the ubiquitous "stringify nested field → STRING column" step is available (via SQL today, or the proposed json_encode inbuilt transform). "Partial" report streams: a faucet upsert/overwrite can produce a correct table, but matching the tap's exact historical accumulation depends on its BigQuery delete-window behaviour.

02What the SQL transform unlocks

You asked specifically what SQL buys. These are the reshapes no inbuilt transform does, but DuckDB (reference tables + recursive CTEs + pivot/unpivot) does — so they count as supported, flagged:

Wide → long unpivot

  • deel — gross-to-net dynamic column map → tall rows
  • sharepoint / onedrive — timeseries period-header sheet → long
  • personio — v1 custom-report attribute pivot

Reference-table joins

  • hibob — named-list ID → human-readable label
  • anthropic — api_key_costs priced against a rate table
  • bamboohr — /meta/fields field aliasing

Report-tree / matrix flatten

  • rillet — balance-sheet tree → leaf rows (heaviest)
  • quickbooks / xero — Rows/Columns report matrix → rows
  • attio — value-map → one row per (record, attribute)
  • ukg_pro — job × compensation × employment cross-join

A tiny inbuilt json_encode/stringify transform would move the ~everyone "stringify nested" case out of SQL entirely; only the genuine reshapes above would then need SQL.

03What only WASM could do — so it does not count

Per your rule, anything reachable only via WASM is left uncounted. Across all 46 taps there is essentially one such case:

not counted Binary file decode in-stream

  • oracle_fusion returns a base64-encoded XLSX inside a SOAP body; reproducing it means base64-decode → parse an XLSX binary mid-pipeline. SQL can't; only arbitrary code (WASM) could — so it stays Blocked.

Not a transform problem at all

  • Custom request signing (skyslope HMAC) and multi-step session login (sap, acumatica, bullhorn, sage) happen at request time — neither SQL nor WASM touches them. They need an auth provider, not a transform (§04 item 1).
  • Async job APIs (salesforce bulk, stripe reports) and runtime stream synthesis (hubspot) are transport/planning gaps — again outside transform scope.

04What to build for full parity

Re-ordered for the new rules. The old "#1 = rebuild the BigQuery sink for _sdc" is gone. The real unlocks are now source-side.

  1. Session / multi-step / signing auth provider — unlocks sap · acumatica · bullhorn · syteline · sage · skyslope

    A provider that runs a login pre-flight (capturing a token / cookie / dynamic base-URL) and can compute a per-request signature (custom HMAC). Modelled on the existing oauth2_refresh provider. Biggest single source-side unlock.

  2. Bookmark → request-parameter injection — server-side incremental for many taps

    Flow the stored bookmark into a query param / filter (OData $filter, Lucene range, gte|, If-Modified-Since). Today faucet filters incremental client-side; several taps need the server-side form to match row counts.

  3. Inbuilt json_encode transform — removes the SQL dependency for most rows

    One transform that JSON-stringifies a nested field to a STRING column. Cheap, and it moves the ubiquitous "stringify nested" step out of SQL, keeping ~most Needs-SQL rows inbuilt-only.

  4. Async-job source pattern — salesforce bulk · stripe reports

    A source shape that submits a job, polls, and downloads the result (CSV). Larger effort; only two taps genuinely require it.

  5. Report-stream decoupling recipe — quickbooks · xero · zohobooks · sage report streams

    These taps DELETE a rolling window from BigQuery then re-append. Provide a keyed-upsert / partition-overwrite recipe so the destination converges without the connector reaching into the warehouse. (Correct table; byte-identical history depends on the window semantics.)

  6. Optional _faucet_* metadata columns — your idea · filed as #510

    Not required for parity (you dropped _sdc), but a good faucet-native lineage feature: an opt-in sink decorator stamping _faucet_extracted_at / _faucet_loaded_at / _faucet_run_id / _faucet_source. Filed as an enhancement.

  7. BigQuery type-mapping + partition/cluster options — sink polish

    Match z3z1ma's type rules (integer+string→STRING, JSON fallback) and let the sink set time-partition + clustering on load. Minor.

05Suggested rollout

Roughly two-thirds of the fleet is reachable now with connectors + transforms; the tail is gated by the auth/transport work above.

Wave 1 Supported — 20

Stock connector + inbuilt transforms. Mostly full-refresh overwrite — easiest to prove identical.

  • ramp, brex, invoiced, redshift, ms365fno, ms365bc, netsuite_pro, afas, dualentry, deskera, restaurant365, campfire, adp, isolved, paylocity, rippling, greenhouse, lever, navan, openai

Wave 2 Needs SQL — 10

Same, plus one DuckDB SQL transform for the named reshape. Fine by your rules.

  • anthropic, sharepointsites, onedrive, bamboohr, hibob, personio, ukg_pro, deel, attio, rillet

Wave 3 Partial — 12

Need the session/signing auth provider, or their report streams are BigQuery-coupled (entities migrate now).

  • sap, syteline, acumatica, shopify, plaid, bullhorn, skyslope, netsuite, quickbooks*, xero*, zohobooks*, sage* (*entity streams now; report streams need decoupling)

Hold Blocked — 4

Keep on Meltano until the async-job pattern lands, or accept a non-identical rebuild.

  • salesforce (bulk API), stripe (SDK + events + reports), hubspot (runtime streams + BigQuery side-channel), oracle_fusion (SOAP + XLSX)

Method — each of the 46 DrivetrainAi/tap-* repositories was read directly (transport, auth, pagination, stream/fan-out model, incremental strategy, in-tap record shaping), alongside the shared target-bigquery fork and faucet-sink-bigquery's own load/overwrite/merge code. Scoring rules per your instruction: _sdc_* ignored; inbuilt transforms and the DuckDB SQL transform count; WASM does not; auth/transport/coupling gaps are not transform-solvable. Verdicts describe reproducing each tap's output table, not merely calling the same API.

Updated at the same URL: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/8af1e9fd-2eb6-497d-a7ad-5a3b16fa004d**

Here's how your three points reshaped it:

**1. `_sdc_` columns ignored** — and that collapses the sink concern. faucet-sink-bigquery already loads via BigQuery load jobs (`CREATE_IF_NEEDED`), does the overwrite = staged truncate-swap, MERGE upsert, and schema-evolution. With `_sdc_` off the table and column-naming moved to the source, the sink is **no longer the blocker** — only two minor follow-ups remain (match z3z1ma's type rules, expose partition/cluster config).

**2. Column-name transforms via inbuilt features** — yes. `flatten` → `parent_child`, `keys_case` → snake_case, `rename_keys`/`rename_field` for aliases, `set` for injected columns, `cast` for epoch↔timestamp. So naming/flattening stop being blockers, which is why the "Supported" set jumped from 3 → **20**. One gap: JSON-stringifying a nested field has no inbuilt transform, so it currently falls to SQL — I flagged a one-line `json_encode` transform (build item #3) that would keep those rows inbuilt-only.

**3. SQL counts (flagged), WASM doesn't.** New scoring — **20 Supported / 10 Needs-SQL / 12 Partial / 4 Blocked** (30 of 46 reachable with connectors + inbuilt/SQL transforms). §02 lists exactly **what SQL unlocks**: wide→long unpivot (deel, sharepoint/onedrive timeseries, personio), reference-table joins (hibob labels, anthropic pricing, bamboohr aliases), report-tree/matrix flatten (rillet, qbo/xero, attio, ukg cross-join). §03 lists the **only WASM-territory case** — `oracle_fusion`'s base64-XLSX-inside-SOAP decode, which SQL can't express, so it stays Blocked and uncounted.

Key honest takeaway: with your rules, **the remaining non-green rows are not shaping problems** — they're auth (session-login / custom HMAC: sap, acumatica, bullhorn, syteline, sage, skyslope), transport (bulk/SDK: salesforce, stripe; SOAP-XLSX: oracle_fusion), runtime stream synthesis (hubspot), or report streams coupled to a mid-sync BigQuery `DELETE` (quickbooks/xero/zohobooks/sage). SQL and WASM don't fix those — an auth provider, an async-job source, and report-decoupling do (build list §04).

**On `_faucet_*` columns — good idea, filed it: #510.** An opt-in sink decorator stamping `_faucet_extracted_at` / `_faucet_loaded_at` / `_faucet_run_id` / `_faucet_source`. Not needed for parity (since you dropped `_sdc`), but genuinely useful for freshness/lineage/incident triage without coupling the connector to the destination — which is exactly the anti-pattern that blocks the accounting taps. I scoped it as a connector-agnostic decorator (like the cleanup tracker) so every sink benefits.

Great framing — the test is "does it unlock a *class*, not a connector." I went back through all 46 taps and clustered the non-green rows by their *root cause*, not their vendor. Seven root causes cover essentially everything, and each maps to one real framework primitive. Here they are, ordered by leverage.

## 1. A composable auth-flow provider *(the single biggest unlock)*
Today `AuthProvider` is single-step (bearer / oauth2 / oauth2_refresh / oauth1 / token-endpoint). The recurring wall is **auth that is a small program**: log in, capture something, place it somewhere, maybe sign each request.

Make auth a **declarative flow** with four composable pieces:
- **pre-flight chain** — run request(s), extract token / cookie / *dynamic base-URL* via JSONPath (`bullhorn` refresh→access→login→`BhRestToken`+`restUrl`; `sap`/`acumatica` cookie login; `sage` session; `personio` `/v1/auth` envelope).
- **credential placement** — header / query / **body** / cookie, via a template (`plaid` creds-in-body, `afas` `AfasToken`, `zoho` `Zoho-oauthtoken`, `ukg` dual header, `campfire` `Token `).
- **pluggable request signer** — a signing hook (`skyslope` custom HMAC; and it generalizes to AWS SigV4, Azure SAS later).
- **refresh + rotation + single-flight** — already have the bones (#499).

**Unlocks / hardens:** sap, acumatica, bullhorn, sage, syteline, skyslope → out of Partial; plus cleaner plaid/afas/zoho/ukg/campfire/personio/netsuite. Auth is universal, so this is the least "hacky" thing on the list.

## 2. A first-class OData source
Six taps are OData that we're currently hand-rolling on `rest` (`sap`, `ms365bc`, `ms365fno`, `netsuite_pro`, `restaurant365`, `acumatica`). OData is a *standard* — a dedicated source handles `@odata.nextLink`, `$filter`/`$orderby`/`$expand`, the `{value}` unwrap (acumatica), and `$metadata` (EDMX) → schema/stream discovery, once. It turns "6 fiddly configs + notes" into "6 clean rows," and every future OData ERP is free.

## 3. Server-side incremental push-down (state → request binding)
faucet tracks bookmarks but filters **client-side**. ~15 taps push the bookmark into the request (`greenhouse` `gte|`, OData `$filter ge`, `bullhorn` Lucene range, `xero` `If-Modified-Since` header, `ms365*` `SysModified`, `netsuite` `lastmodifieddate`, `shopify` query DSL…). Add a small **binding spec**: "render the stored bookmark into `{query param | header | body field | path}` with this operator template; advance from this response field." Generalizes to *every* incremental API and fixes row-count parity + cost.

## 4. An async-job source pattern (submit → poll → fetch)
A whole class of "big data" APIs is submit-a-job / poll-status / download-result: `salesforce` Bulk, `stripe` reports, plus (future) Amplitude/Mixpanel/Google-Ads/warehouse-unload exports. A first-class 3-phase source (submit → poll on a status JSONPath with terminal states → fetch result URL) turns two Blocked rows into Supported and is a reusable primitive for dozens of connectors we don't have yet.

## 5. A response-decode pipeline on sources
Right now the body must be JSON (or, via #497, a CSV/Excel file). Make decoding a **declarative chain**: extract a field (JSONPath) → base64-decode → gunzip/unzip → parse (json / csv / xlsx / xml). That unlocks `oracle_fusion` (base64-XLSX-in-SOAP — the *only* WASM-territory case today), and it's exactly what bulk/report results need (they're usually zipped CSV). Pairs with #4.

## 6. Three inbuilt reshape transforms — to delete the SQL dependency
You want fewer SQL rows. Almost every "Needs SQL" case is one of three shapes:
- **`unpivot`** (map / wide → long): `deel` gross-to-net, `attio` value-map, `personio` pivot, `sharepoint` timeseries.
- **`lookup` / `enrich`** (join a small reference set fetched once → add label columns): `hibob` named-lists, `anthropic` pricing, `bamboohr` field aliases. (Reuses the #501 discovery machinery as the reference source.)
- **`json_encode`** (stringify a nested field): the ubiquitous one.

Ship these three inbuilt and **the "Needs SQL" column basically empties** — only genuinely bespoke arithmetic would remain, and even that (anthropic pricing) becomes `lookup` + `set`.

## 7. Self-describing stream/schema discovery
Generalize #211 (DB catalog) + #501 (value discovery) into **"discover streams + schemas from a metadata endpoint"**: OData `$metadata`, `afas` `/metainfo`, `hubspot` `/schemas` custom objects, `bamboohr`/`personio`/`ukg` report+UDF metadata, `sharepoint`'s per-file manifest. This is the primitive behind hubspot's "runtime-synthesized streams" done declaratively — the API describes itself, we generate the matrix.

---

**Bonus (sink side): scoped/windowed overwrite.** The accounting taps (`quickbooks`/`xero`/`zohobooks`/`sage` reports, and `hubspot`) reach *into* BigQuery to `DELETE` a rolling window before re-appending. Add a **`write_mode: overwrite` scoped to a window/key** ("replace only rows matching this run's scope") — the same idea as #478 scoped cleanup, applied to writes. That removes the tap↔warehouse coupling entirely and is a real primitive for any rolling-window/report load.

## Net effect
These 7 (+1) are orthogonal primitives, not patches. Together they'd move the fleet from **~30/46 reachable to ~44/46 Supported**, and #6 alone **eliminates almost all SQL**. The only genuine residual is truly one-off logic (very rare). Sequencing by leverage: **#1 auth-flow → #6 reshape transforms → #3 incremental push-down → #2 OData source → #4+#5 async-job+decode → #7 discovery → scoped overwrite.**

Want me to file these as tracked epics on `faucet-hq/faucet-stream` (cross-linked to the roadmap #38), and add a "first-class primitives" section to the artifact? I'd file #1, #3, and #6 as the top-priority trio since they unblock the most with the least surface area.

## Summary
Turn `AuthProvider` from a single-step credential source into a **composable, declarative auth flow**: an optional login/pre-flight request chain, arbitrary credential placement (header / query / body / cookie), a pluggable per-request signer, and dynamic base-URL capture — on top of the existing refresh/rotation/single-flight machinery.

## Motivation
This is the single biggest source-side unlock found in the Meltano→faucet parity analysis (`DrivetrainAi/meltano_taps`, 46 taps). The recurring wall is not the transport — it's that auth is a *small program*. Current providers (static / bearer / oauth2 / oauth2_refresh / oauth1 / token-endpoint) are all single-step and place the credential in a fixed spot. First-class auth flows move a whole class of connectors from **Partial → Supported** and keep it out of per-connector hacks. Ties to the Primary Goal (reliability) and Third-Party Connector Friendliness (auth handled in `faucet-core`/`faucet-auth`, not re-implemented per connector).

Concrete taps unblocked / hardened: **sap** (session cookie), **acumatica** (cookie login + 401 re-login), **bullhorn** (refresh→access→login→`BhRestToken` + dynamic `restUrl`), **sage/intacct** (session pool), **syteline** (Infor ION password grant), **skyslope** (custom HMAC signing + session), plus cleaner **plaid** (creds-in-body), **afas** (`AfasToken`), **zohobooks** (`Zoho-oauthtoken`), **ukg_pro** (Basic + custom API-key header), **campfire** (`Token ` prefix), **personio** (`/v1/auth` JSON envelope).

## Proposed design (sketch — needs design discussion)
A declarative `flow` on the shared `auth:` catalog, built by `faucet-auth` and consumed via `Source::with_auth_provider` (unchanged trait):
```yaml
auth:
  bullhorn:
    type: flow
    steps:                              # pre-flight chain; each captures values by JSONPath
      - request: { method: POST, url: "${env:AUTH_HOST}/oauth/token", form: { grant_type: refresh_token, refresh_token: "${env:RT}" } }
        capture: { access_token: "$.access_token", refresh_token: "$.refresh_token" }
      - request: { method: GET, url: "${env:LOGIN_HOST}/rest-services/login", query: { access_token: "${access_token}" } }
        capture: { bh_rest_token: "$.BhRestToken", base_url: "$.restUrl" }   # dynamic base-URL
    apply:                              # credential placement (header|query|body|cookie)
      - { in: query, name: BhRestToken, value: "${bh_rest_token}" }
    base_url_from: base_url            # override the connector's base_url per session
    rotate: { refresh_token: { persist: { path: ... } } }   # reuse #499
    ttl_secs: 86400
    reauth_on: [401]
```
- **Signer hook**: `apply: [{ sign: { alg: hmac_sha256, key: "${env:SECRET}", template: "{client_id}:{client_secret}:{ts}", into: { header: Authorization, format: "SS {access_key}:{sig}" } } }]` — a `RequestSigner` trait so HMAC variants (and later AWS SigV4 / Azure SAS) are pluggable.
- **Credential placement enum**: `Header | Query | BodyField | Cookie`, templated.
- **Dynamic base-URL**: a provider may return a per-session base URL the source uses instead of its configured one (bullhorn, zoho region).

`crates/core/src/auth.rs` (add `RequestSigner` trait + a `sign_request`/placement hook — the object-safe defaulted method already exists from #292/#496 groundwork), `crates/auth/` (new `flow` provider + signer impls), `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (build `type: flow`), the rest/xml/graphql sources (honor dynamic base-URL + apply-placement), docs.

## Edge cases & failure modes
Re-auth storm on shared token (single-flight); cookie vs header session; capture path missing → typed error; rotated-token persistence race (reuse #499); signer clock skew; redaction of captured secrets (reuse `secrets::registry`).

## Acceptance criteria
Multi-step login + capture + placement + one HMAC signer, exercised end-to-end against a wiremock login→data flow; dynamic base-URL honored; unit tests on the pure capture/placement/signing logic; ≥90% patch coverage.

## Out of scope (v1)
Browser/interactive OAuth consent; SAML.

## References
Meltano→faucet parity analysis. Builds on #496 (oauth1 HMAC), #499 (refresh persistence). Roadmap epic #38.
